name: India Glycols Ltd
title: India Glycols Ltd - 500201 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: India Glycols FY26 net revenue rose 11.8% to INR4,211 crores, with EBITDA up 24.5% to INR654 crores and margin at 15.5%.
summary.overview: FY26 showed strong operating performance: gross revenue INR9,827 crores (+8.7%), net revenue INR4,211 crores (+11.8%), EBITDA INR654 crores (+24.5%) and PAT INR293 crores (+26.8%). Q4 net revenue rose 13.1% to INR976 crores with EBITDA of INR167 crores (+13.3%). Bio-Fuels and Chemicals drove margin gains, while Chemicals sales fell and Ennature Biopharma margins stayed under pressure. Management said the Middle East war had a mixed but slightly positive effect via ethanol competitiveness, though export business to the Middle East was on hold. Debt was reduced by prepaying about INR804 crores in the quarter, including INR467 crores from a November 2025 equity issue.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: FY26 net revenue INR1,203 crores (-10.4%), EBIT INR141 crores (+12.5%), EBIT margin 11.7%. Q4 net revenue INR301 crores (+18.8%), EBIT INR37 crores (+37.4%), margin 12.2%.

segments.name: Potable Spirits (IMFL + IMIL)
segments.commentary: FY26 top-line INR1,331 crores (+14.4%), EBIT INR285 crores (+11.1%). Q4 top-line INR306 crores (+7.9%), EBIT INR68 crores, margin 22.1%. IMFL is about 31% of segment revenue per management, with Amrut about 5-6%.

segments.name: Bio-Fuels
segments.commentary: FY26 top-line INR1,470 crores (+40.9%), EBIT INR115 crores (+103.3%), margin 7.8%. Q4 top-line INR305 crores (+11.6%), EBIT INR30 crores (+90.0%), margin 9.9%.

segments.name: Ennature Biopharma
segments.commentary: FY26 top-line broadly flat with a nominal decline, margins under pressure. Q4 top-line grew 23.2%, but EBIT was only INR3 crores.

guidance_outlook: Management expects improved profitability and top-line growth in Chemicals for FY27, and expects performance chemicals to more than double in FY27 (hoped, not projected).

Interest cost expected to stay around INR25 crores per quarter; FY27 scheduled term-loan repayment about INR268 crores (liquor INR168 crores, chemicals INR100 crores), plus further prepayments of high-cost debt.
Management expects the JV share of profit to improve drastically from FY26 INR46.42 crores as 49% JV is consolidated into the Chemicals business.
Plan to sell a further 24% JV equity in FY28-29 per agreement, proceeds to repay term loans and make the Chemical business debt-free by FY28-29 (hoped).

Management aims for high double-digit IMFL growth via geographic expansion (Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan) and new brands; no formal margin guidance for Potable Spirits beyond Q4's 22% EBIT margin.
capex_capacity: Capex of about INR830 crores in FY26, with about INR600 crores spent in the last six months; about INR400 crores capitalised from grain distilleries at Gorakhpur and Kashipur.
Plant shutdown from 17 March to 2 April 2026 for catalyst change, reducing production and some sales; EO supply to the Clariant JV stopped for 15-20 days.
Ethanol capacity now slightly exceeds in-house Bio-Fuels consumption; grain-based (dual feedstock) ethanol flexibility retained.
Ennature Biopharma investing in manufacturing capability and branded nutraceutical clinical studies, with some studies to complete in FY27.
demand_pricing: Potable Spirits: IMIL is about 75% of segment volume but about 52% of UP value; IMFL is about 16% of UP volume and 34% of value. IMFL volumes grew 30% in the year, with UP IMFL top-line growth of 25% last year.
IMIL growth was 21% in Uttarakhand and 11% in UP; Amazing Vodka reached a 21% market share in Uttarakhand vs 18% last year.
Bacardi bottling revenue sits in miscellaneous income, with filling charges estimated at 2-3% of Potable revenue.
Grain prices fell from about INR24/kg mid-2025 to about INR21-22/kg in Q4 FY26; DDGS prices improved.

Imported ethanol prices rose sharply on freight and other factors, while domestic prices were stable or slightly lower; the Middle East war raised crude and constrained MEG and ethanol availability, which improved ethanol-based product competitiveness.
Oilfield chemical exports to the Middle East, largely for New Park, are on hold due to the war; propylene oxide prices and availability were also affected.
Chemicals sales declined due to Chinese low-cost glycol ethers, weaker gases sales after argon price spikes, and lower EO sales to the JV when EO was uncompetitive versus Reliance.

qa_highlights.question: How was business disturbed by the plant shutdown, and what is the Potable Spirits split and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Shutdown for catalyst change (about every 1.5 years) affected EO supply to the Clariant JV and some specialty products, not MEG. IMFL is about 25% and IMIL about 75% of Potable Spirits (Raju Vaziraney, although later data cite IMFL at 31% of revenue). Management did not guide to a margin number, saying Q4's 22% EBIT margin is not assured to be sustained.

qa_highlights.question: Why did BSPC/Chemicals top-line decline, and are plants at optimal level?
qa_highlights.answer: Glycol ethers lost share to cheaper Chinese and propylene/butylene-based material, gases declined on high argon prices in the prior year, and EO sales to the JV fell. Management expects improved profitability and top-line growth in FY27 and said the large EO price delta with Reliance has narrowed.

qa_highlights.question: Why was JV profit INR13 crores in Q4 and what is the JV monetisation plan?
qa_highlights.answer: JV profit improved on mix and imported traded materials from Clariant; FY26 share of profit was INR46.42 crores vs INR46.40 crores. The company plans to sell a further 24% equity in FY28-29 per the agreement to repay term loans and make Chemicals debt-free.

qa_highlights.question: Finance cost run-rate and FY27 debt repayment?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR804 crores prepaid in Q4 (INR467 crores from promoter equity, rest internal cash). Interest cost to stay around INR25 crores per quarter. FY27 scheduled repayment is INR268 crores (liquor INR168 crores, chemicals INR100 crores), plus prepayments.

qa_highlights.question: Silver sale during shutdown and grain availability?
qa_highlights.answer: Silver sold for INR98 crores against purchase cost of INR51 crores; no profit was booked because catalyst consumption was not yet provided. Grain stocks are adequate and prices are stable; grain was about 73% of ethanol feedstock in FY26 with maize about 46%.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the Ennature Biopharma outlook and nicotine pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is shifting nicotine to value-added long-term customers and diversifying into branded nutraceuticals with clinical studies. EBITDA improvement may not show in FY27 despite customer acquisition.

risks_watch: Middle East war: export business for oilfield chemicals on hold; propylene oxide availability and prices affected; demand softening in some areas.
Ennature Biopharma margins under pressure from nicotine price competition and the Thiocolchicoside price cycle; EBIT was only INR3 crores in Q4.
Bio-Fuels profitability depends on government blending policy (20% achieved; talk of higher blending and flex-fuel) and feedstock prices.
Pending NCLT-approved demerger of a division; order expected around 21 May 2026 with a possible June 2026 order.
Chemicals volume recovery depends on JV EO offtake, which was affected by the shutdown and the Reliance price gap.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the full year and on premiumisation and ethanol, but evasive on specifics: margin guidance, JV exit timing and the Amrut and Bacardi economics were deferred or left undisclosed. Cautious on Chemicals and Ennature, where management said results will improve but gave few numbers.
key_quotes: So whilst, if you remember when we started doing these calls, we spoke about certain challenges that the business had and a strategy to overcome those challenges both in terms of actions in the marketplace, diversifying our portfolio, taking some cost actions.
And as I have already told that in '28-'29, we are going to sell out 24% more equity as per the agreement.

Right now, to a large extent that has been adjusted, and we believe that the huge delta that we saw for a period of one-and-a- half-two years, hopefully in my opinion, maybe a thing of the past and we should see much better competitiveness on that front as well.

adds.what: Grain distilleries at Gorakhpur and Kashipur (about INR400 crores capitalised of INR830 crores FY26 capex)

growth.why: Management hopes performance chemicals more than double in FY27 (not projected) and targets high double-digit IMFL growth via Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Rajasthan expansion, backed by ~INR400 crores of recently capitalised grain distilleries, but no specific order book or revenue guidance is given.
